acceptance.given: A destructive operation is defined or requested with its affected scope and authorization context available for evaluation.

oracle.expected: The operation documentation or request contains either recovery information or an explicit irreversibility disclosure.
forbidden: The operation provides neither recovery information nor an irreversibility disclosure.
oracle.observable: At the documentation/request boundary, a recovery disclosure or explicit irreversibility disclosure is present.

acceptance.then: The operation records or presents a recovery disclosure or an explicit irreversibility disclosure.
acceptance.when: The destructive-operation contract is evaluated before execution.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the destructive-operation contract case whose recovery_or_irreversibility_disclosure field is absent and assert the pre-execution contract check fails.

affected_subjects: Destructive operation recovery or irreversibility disclosure
slice_hint.behavior_change: Add or verify the pre-execution contract check that requires recovery information or an explicit irreversibility disclosure for every destructive operation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema change; reverting restores prior contract evaluation behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: Destructive operation contract moves from undefined disclosure to disclosure-present or validation failure.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted contract case fails when disclosure is absent and passes when recovery or irreversibility disclosure is supplied.

acceptance.given: A destructive operation request carries confirmation derived solely from untrusted input and has no trusted session, user, or policy-authorized source.

oracle.expected: The operation reports failure and does not proceed.
forbidden: Solely untrusted input is accepted as sufficient confirmation.
The operation proceeds successfully on the basis of solely untrusted confirmation.
oracle.observable: The operation result is a failure at the authorization boundary, with no destructive effect initiated.

acceptance.then: The operation fails because the confirmation source is solely untrusted input.
acceptance.when: The destructive-operation authorization check evaluates the request before any destructive effect.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the destructive-operation case with confirmation supplied only by untrusted input and assert the authorization check returns failure before execution.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject destructive-operation confirmation when its only source is untrusted input.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema change; authorization behavior remains contract-compatible for trusted sources.

slice_hint.state_transition: Request changes from pending destructive execution to authorization failure with no destructive effect.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The untrusted-confirmation selector deterministically fails the operation and confirms no execution side effect.

acceptance.given: A destructive operation request omits its affected-scope declaration.

oracle.expected: The operation reports failure before initiating any destructive effect.
forbidden: A destructive operation with missing scope succeeds.
A destructive effect is initiated despite the missing scope.
oracle.observable: The pre-execution validation result is failure and no destructive action is started.

acceptance.then: The operation fails because no affected scope is declared.
acceptance.when: The destructive-operation request is validated before execution.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the destructive-operation case with an absent affected-scope declaration and assert validation fails before execution.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject destructive-operation requests that do not declare affected scope.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema change; only pre-execution validation is tightened.

slice_hint.state_transition: Request changes from scope-missing to validation failure without starting a destructive effect.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The missing-scope selector deterministically fails and verifies that no destructive action is initiated.

acceptance.given: A destructive operation request includes a bypass flag as the basis for proceeding.

oracle.expected: The operation reports failure before execution and the bypass flag cannot circumvent confirmation or authorization.
forbidden: A bypass flag causes the operation to proceed successfully.
The bypass flag circumvents the required confirmation or authorization control.
oracle.observable: The authorization result is failure and no destructive effect is initiated when bypass is present.

acceptance.then: The operation fails because a bypass flag was supplied.
acceptance.when: The destructive-operation authorization check evaluates the request before execution.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the destructive-operation case containing a bypass flag and assert the authorization check fails before execution.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject destructive-operation requests that attempt to proceed through a bypass flag.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema change; authorization behavior remains schema-compatible.

slice_hint.state_transition: Request changes from bypass-present to authorization failure with no destructive effect.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The bypass-flag selector deterministically fails and confirms required authorization remains enforced.
